question: Why is Shiva described as unfixed, all-pervading, eternal, and universal in form?
premises: Shiva is not fixed or limited.
He is all-pervading and therefore present everywhere.
He is eternal and therefore without beginning or end.
He has the form of the universe.
inference: Because Shiva is all-pervading, eternal, and universal in form, he is not subject to limitation in space, time, or shape.
plain_english: Shiva is not fixed or limited. He is all-pervading and eternal, and he takes the form of the whole universe. Because he pervades everything, he is present everywhere; because he is eternal, he has no beginning or end.
